answer.title: The Pythagorean theorem
answer.summary: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: BC² = AB² + AC² when the right angle is at A.

segments.text: The theorem only works in a right triangle; the hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle.
If AB = 3 and AC = 4 in a triangle right-angled at A, then BC = 5, because 9 + 16 = 25.
We use it to calculate a missing side when we know the other two sides.
The converse of the theorem (used to prove a triangle is right-angled) is a related but different topic, not explained in detail here.

connections.relation: Needed in the last step to get the length from its square.
Calculating a distance on a grid uses the same Pythagorean idea.
Used to check whether a triangle is right-angled.

simplify.title: Pythagoras in simple words
simplify.text: In a triangle with a right angle, if you draw a square on each side, the area of the big square (on the hypotenuse) equals the areas of the two small squares added together.

examples.title: A ladder against a wall
examples.body: A 5 m ladder with its foot 3 m from the wall reaches a height of 4 m.

examples.title: A TV screen
examples.body: A screen's size (in inches) is the length of its diagonal, calculated with Pythagoras from its width and height.

questions.question: When does the Pythagorean theorem apply?
questions.explanation: The theorem is specific to right triangles.

questions.question: A right triangle has sides 6 and 8 next to the right angle. What is the hypotenuse?
What is the hypotenuse?

choices.text: The side opposite the right angle

questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is the longest side.
